rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq escaped punishment by changing ضاع to ضاء, recasting a complaint that his poetry was lost at Khalisa’s door as praise of its radiance.
rows.anchor: وإنما قلت : وخالصة من وراء الستر تسمع : فلقد ضاء شعري على بابكم … كما ضاء در على خالصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khalisa rewarded the poet with more than a million dirhams in jewelry; Sulayman bought the jewelry back and returned it to her.
rows.anchor: فأتبعه سليمان بن عبد الملك حاجبه لما خرج من عنده حتى اشترى الحلي من الفرزدق بما ألف ورده على خالصة

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says Abu Hanifa rejects the separate exception that the caliph’s grandfather permitted.
rows.anchor: هذا يعني أبا حنيفة يخالف جدك حيث يقول : الاستثناء المنفصل جائز وأبو حنيفة ينكره

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa answers the charge by arguing that if people could privately except themselves from a pledge, they could cancel allegiance after returning home.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة هذا الربيع يقول ليس لك بيعة في رقبة الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf conditionally upheld retaliation for a Muslim who killed a protected non-Muslim, requiring proof that the victim was paying jizya; without proof, the claim failed.
rows.anchor: حتى تقوم البينة العادلة أن الذمي يوم قتله المسلم كان ممن يؤدي الجزية فلم يقدروا عليه فبطل دمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghadban’s reply وعليك السلام secured him safety from al-Hajjaj, illustrating the practical benefit of knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقال له ما جواب السلام عليك ؟ فقال وعليك السلام ثم فطن الحجاح ، وقال : قاتلك الله يا غضبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poet escaped danger by parsing the final ر of أمير as accusative, making Shabib the caliph he was addressing rather than the caliph being named.
rows.anchor: فقال : إنما قلت ومنا أمير المؤمنين شبيب ، بنصب الراء فناديتك واستغثت بك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sulayman b. Kathir explained that his curse against Abu Muslim was spoken while looking at unripe grapes; Abu Muslim appreciated the excuse and forgave him.
rows.anchor: ولكن في كرم كذا لما نظرت إلى الحصرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa rules that the spouses can speak without breaking their mutual oaths, since the initial exchange about the oaths had already dissolved them.
rows.anchor: أعاد أبو حنيفة الفتوى ، فقال من أين قلت ؟ قال : لما شافهته باليمين بعدما حلف كانت مكلمة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan praises Abu Hanifa’s analysis as revealing a point of knowledge that everyone else had missed.
rows.anchor: قال سفيان : إنه ليكشف لك من العلم عن شيء كلنا عنه غافل

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa helps a man recover stolen goods despite his oath of silence by having neighbors identify suspects individually; the thief’s silence identifies him.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم أبو حنيفة . هل تحبون أن يرد الله على هذا متاعه ؟ قالوا : نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa lends a young man the unaffordable bride-price and advises him to claim he will move away after the marriage, prompting the in-laws to seek a settlement.
rows.anchor: ثم قال له : بعد الدخول أظهر أنك تريد الخروج من هذا البلد إلى بلد بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa resolves the marriage dispute by suggesting the husband threaten to travel with his wife until her family repays the bride-price; a debt would then prevent her travel, so he accepts a settlement.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : الطريق أن ترضوه بأن تردوا عليه ما أخذتموه منه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa advises a father to buy the slave girl himself and marry her to his son, so a divorce returns her to the father and the son’s attempted emancipation is ineffective.
rows.anchor: فقال له أبو حنيفة : إذهب به معك إلى سوق النخاسين فإذا وقعت عينه على جارية فابتعها لنفسك

rows.speaker: الليث بن سعد
rows.claim: Al-Layth says he admired Abu Hanifa’s quick response even more than its substance.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : فوالله ما أعجبني جوابه كما أعجبني سرعة جوابه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa answers a vow to have intercourse with one’s wife during Ramadan by advising the couple to travel, making daytime intercourse permissible for the traveler.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو حنيفة : يسافر مع امرأته فيطؤها نهارا / في رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Hajjaj tracks the thief of four thousand dirhams through a distinctive perfume and recovers the money for the victim.
rows.anchor: من وجد منه ريح هذا الطيب فخذوه فإذا رجل له وفرة فأخذوه

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf resolves Harun al-Rashid’s problem with an oath not to sell, give away, or free a beloved slave by gifting half and selling half.
rows.anchor: فقال : يهب النصف ويبيع النصف ولايحنث

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحسن
rows.claim: Muhammad b. al-Hasan tells Harun al-Rashid that his fear of God after sin entitles him to two gardens, citing the promise to whoever fears standing before his Lord.
rows.anchor: فقلت له يا أمير المؤمنين إذاوقعت في معصية هل تخاف الله في تلك الحالة أو بعدها

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abu Yusuf frees a slave girl from the caliph’s coercive oath by instructing her to confess when asked whether she stole the jewelry, then deny stealing it when asked to produce it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو يوسف : قد صدقت يا أمير المؤمنين في الإقرار أو الإنكار

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: Shafiʿi defeats Bishr al-Muraysi’s objection that universal consensus cannot be known by asking whether he recognizes consensus on the caliph’s rule; Bishr concedes and falls silent.
rows.anchor: فقال الشافعي : هل تعرف إجماع الناس على خلافة هذا الجالس ؟ فأقر به خوفا وانقطع

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that whoever wishes to see him should look at al-Hasan and al-Husayn.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : إذا أردتم أن تنظروا إلي فانظروا إلى الحسن والحسين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says a person’s worth is measured by what he excels at.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسين سمعت أبي عليا يقول قيمة كل امرىء ما يحسنه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Husayn attributes to his grandfather the maxim that generosity should be proportionate to the recipient’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: وسمعت جدي يقول : المعروف بقدر المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Husayn’s test, the Bedouin names faith as the best deed, trust in God as rescue from ruin, and knowledge with forbearance as adornment; generosity, patience, or a lightning strike follow if those are absent.
rows.anchor: قال الأعرابي : الإيمان بالله . قال : فما نجاة العبد من الهلكة قال : الثقة بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is intrinsically noble and beloved, while ignorance is intrinsically deficient: the learned are hurt by being called ignorant, and the ignorant pleased by false praise as learned.
rows.anchor: وكل ذلك دليل على أن العلم شريف لذاته ومحبوب لذاته والجهل نقصان لذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge naturally commands deference: animals check themselves before humans, ordinary people follow the more capable, and even the Prophet’s enemies were awed into submission; the cited poem says his bearing itself told his story.
rows.anchor: فلو لم تكن فيه آيات مبينة … كانت بداهتة تنبيك عن خبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human superiority over other animals comes from a divine, luminous faculty that enables grasping truths and worship, not from strength; humanity’s purpose is worship.
rows.anchor: واللطيفة الربانية التي لأجلها صار مستعدا لإدراك حقائق الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The learned mind ranges across all categories and relations of being, and a knowledgeable soul can bring ignorant souls to knowledge, becoming complete and then perfecting others as an intermediary between God and people.
rows.anchor: فإنها كانت كاملة ثم صارت مكملة وتصير واسطة بين الله وبين عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes interpret the Spirit sent with the angels and the Spirit revealed to Muhammad as knowledge or the Qur’an; just as a body without spirit is dead, spirit without knowledge is dead.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون فسروا هذا الروح بالعلم والقرآن وكما أن البدن بلا روح ميت فاسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge is the spirit of spirit and enduring happiness because universal conceptions do not decay or change.
rows.anchor: فالعلم روح الروح ونور النور ولب اللب ومن خواص هذه السعادة أنها تكون باقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets were sent to call people to truth, using wisdom and clear insight as the Qur’an commands.
rows.anchor: فالأنبياء صلوات الله عليهم ما بعثوا إلا للدعوة إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the exchange with the angels, God answers their concern about human corruption by saying He knows what they do not, setting knowledge itself as the relevant answer.
rows.anchor: لما قال : { إني جاعل فى الارض خليفة } ( البقرة : 30 ) قالت الملائكة : { أتجعل فيها من يفسد فيها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers the angels through knowledge rather than power, will, hearing, sight, or other attributes, showing knowledge’s superior rank among divine perfections.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل صفة العلم جوابا لهم وذلك يدل على أن صفات الجلال والكمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God displayed Adam’s superiority by knowledge, then made him the object of the angels’ prostration and the deputy of the lower world; knowledge earned that distinction.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه سبحانه إنما أظهر فضل آدم عليه السلام بالعلم وذلك يدل أيضا على أن العلم أشرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ glorification is praiseworthy only when joined with knowledge; without it, worship would be hypocrisy or blameworthy imitation.
rows.anchor: فإنهما إن حصلا بدون العلم كان ذلك نفاقا والنفاق أخس المراتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam’s single ijtihadi error had grave consequences, which Razi treats as evidence of the great stakes and exalted rank of knowledge.
rows.anchor: إنما وقع عليه اسم المعصية لأنه أخطأ / في مسألة واحدة اجتهادية على ما سيأتي بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through knowledge Adam repented, abandoned persistence and pride, and received the honor of divine election.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه ببركة جلالة العلم لما تاب وأناب وترك الإصرار والاستكبار وجد خلعة الاجتباء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham reasoned from the star to the moon and sun, reached the Creator through proof, and received God’s praise for his insight and argument.
rows.anchor: ولم يزل ينتقل بفكره من شيء إلى شيء إلى أن وصل بالدليل الزاهر والبرهان الباهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After learning about the Creator, Abraham sought knowledge of resurrection, then taught and argued with his father, his people, and the ruler of his time.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه عليه السلام بعد الفراغ من معرفة المبدأ اشتغل بمعرفة المعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The careers of Salih, Hud, Shuʿayb, and Moses likewise show prophets learning, teaching, and directing people to examine evidence.
rows.anchor: كيف كان اشتغالهم في أوائل أمورهم وأواخرها بالتعلم والتعليم وإرشاد الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s gifts to Muhammad include guidance and knowledge before material wealth; the sequence and the references to what he did not know exalt knowledge.
rows.anchor: فقدم الامتنان بالعلم على الامتنان بالمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhammad’s first revelation began with the command to read, and God then taught him what he had not known.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه أول ما أوحى إليه قال : { اقرأ باسم ربك } ( العلق : 1 ) ثم قال : { وعلمك ما لم تكن تعلم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet would pray to be shown things as they truly are.
rows.anchor: وهو عليه الصلاة والسلام كان أبدا يقول : أرنا الأشياء كما هي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an dignifies knowledge by naming it life, spirit, and light.
rows.anchor: سمى العلم في كتابه بالأسماء الشريفة . فمنها : الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Talut’s selection over the people is supported by his greater knowledge and physical capacity, with knowledge named first.
rows.anchor: إن الله اصطفاه عليكم وزاده بسطة في العلم والجسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks to manage the land’s storehouses on the basis of being trustworthy and knowledgeable, rather than lineage, eloquence, or beauty.
rows.anchor: وقال يوسف { اجعلنى على خزائن الارض إنى حفيظ عليم } ( يوسف : 55 ) ولم يقل إني حسيب نسيب فصيح مليح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported saying locates a person’s distinction in the heart and tongue: speech uses the tongue, while combat uses the heart.
rows.anchor: جاء في الخبر ( المرء بأصغريه قلبه ولسانه ) إن تكلم تكلم بلسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poet says a young man is half tongue and half heart, leaving only flesh and blood as the remainder.
rows.anchor: لسان الفتى نصف ونصف فؤاده … فلم يبق إلا صورة اللحم والدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an presents being veiled from God as a punishment before the punishment of Hell.
rows.anchor: فقال : { كلا إنهم عن ربهم يومئذ لمحجوبون * ثم إنهم لصالوا الجحيم } ( المطففين : 15 ، 16 )

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say knowledge has three points of origin: a thinking heart, an expressive tongue, and an illustrative explanation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : العلوم مطالعها من ثلاثة أوجه ، قلب متفكر ، ولسان معبر

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali offers a wordplay defining the letters of العلم through elevation, subtlety, and magnanimity.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه : ( عين العلم من العلو ، ولامه من اللطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A list presented as ten sciences assigns practical purposes to theology, esoteric knowledge, social conduct, law, astronomy, combat, politics, dream interpretation, physiognomy, medicine, and divine reality.
rows.anchor: وأيضا قيل العلوم عشرة : علم التوحيد للأديان ، وعلم السر لرد الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A four-water analogy links kinds of knowledge to the Qur’anic water from heaven: theology to spring water, jurisprudence to a canal, asceticism to rain, and innovations to destructive floodwater.
rows.anchor: وأيضا قيل ضرب المثل في العلم بالماء قوله تعالى : { أنزل من السماء مآء }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Theology resembles spring water that should not be disturbed; seeking to know God’s manner risks unbelief.
rows.anchor: علم التوحيد كماء العين لا يجوز تحريكه لئلا يتكدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurisprudence resembles canal water that increases through digging, as legal understanding grows through inference.
rows.anchor: وعلم الفقه يزداد بالاستنباط كماء القناة يزداد بالحفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ascetic knowledge resembles clear rainwater that becomes clouded by air, as asceticism is clouded by greed.
rows.anchor: وعلم الزهد كماء المطر ينزل صافيا ويتكدر بغبار الهواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innovation resembles a flood that kills living things and destroys people.
rows.anchor: وعلم البدع كماء السيل يميت الأحياء ويهلك الخلق

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأشعري
rows.claim: Al-Ashʿari defines knowledge as that by which one knows, or that which makes an essence knowing.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأشعري العلم ما يعلم به وربما قال ما يصير الذات به عالما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi reports the objection that al-Ashʿari’s definition is circular because knower and known are understood only through knowledge, then gives al-Ashʿari’s reply from immediate self-knowledge of knowing, pain, and pleasure.
rows.anchor: واعترضوا عليه بأن العالم والمعلوم لا يعرفان إلا بالعلم

rows.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
rows.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr defines knowledge as knowing an object as it is, or simply as maʿrifa.
rows.anchor: وقال القاضي أبو بكر العلم معرفة المعلوم على ما هو عليه وربما قال العلم هو المعرفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi objects that defining knowledge as knowing the known is circular, and that “as it is” adds nothing after saying knowledge conforms to the object.
rows.anchor: والاعتراض على الأول أن قوله معرفة المعلوم تعريف العلم بالمعلوم فيعود الدور أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects identifying knowledge with maʿrifa as tautological; maʿrifa follows ambiguity and cannot describe God because it presupposes prior ignorance.
rows.anchor: وثالثها : أن الله تعالى يوصف بأنه عالم ولا يوصف بأنه عارف لأن المعرفة تستدعي سبق الجهل

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني
rows.claim: Al-Isfarayini defines knowledge as disclosing the known, making realities manifest, or simply clarification.
rows.anchor: وقال الأستاذ أبو إسحاق الإسفرايني : العلم تبيين المعلوم وربما قال إنه استبانة الحقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says clarification is merely a harder word substituted for knowledge, and disclosure after obscurity does not apply to God; the fuller definition inherits al-Qadi’s objections.
rows.anchor: وهو أيضا ضعيف أما قول العلم هو التبيين فليس فيه إلا تبديل لفظ بلفظ أخفى منه

rows.speaker: الأستاذ أبو بكر بن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Furak defines knowledge as that which enables its possessor to perform and perfect an act.
rows.anchor: قال الأستاذ أبو بكر بن فورك : العلم ما يصح من المتصف به / إحكام الفعل وإتقانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi objects that this account cannot cover knowledge of necessary truths or impossibilities, which do not produce perfected action.
rows.anchor: لأن العلم بوجوب الواجبات وامتناع الممتنعات لا يفيد الأحكام

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal defines knowledge as affirming the known as it is, or conceiving the known as it is.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال : العلم إثبات المعلوم على ما هو به وربما قيل العلم تصور المعلوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the objections already given apply to al-Qaffal’s formulations as well.
rows.anchor: والوجوه السالفة متوجهة على هذه العبارة

rows.speaker: إمام الحرمين
rows.claim: Al-Juwayni sorts belief into certain or uncertain: matching certainty is immediate, theoretical, or unsupported imitation; false certainty is ignorance; equal uncertainty is doubt, while its stronger and weaker sides are expectation and illusion.
rows.anchor: وقال إمام الحرمين : الطريق إلى تصور ماهية العلم وتميزها عن غيرها أن نقول إنا نجد من أنفسنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says al-Juwayni’s account is flawed in several respects, with the specific objections deferred beyond this excerpt.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التعريف مختل من وجوه
